stories.title: India’s FY28 fiscal deficit projected at 4.3% of GDP
stories.summary: Deutsche Bank projects that India’s fiscal deficit will remain at 4.3 % of GDP in FY 2028. The outlook notes that consolidation is hampered by rising government expenditure and higher subsidy outlays. The bank also forecasts GDP growth of 7.3 % for FY 27 and 7.2 % for FY 28, while retail inflation has risen above the RBI’s upper tolerance band, driven mainly by food prices.

stories.title: Mutual funds raise stakes in 16 small‑cap firms as 11 record steep one‑year declines
stories.summary: Over the four quarters ending September 2026, mutual funds increased their holdings in about 16 Nifty Smallcap 250 companies with market capitalisation above Rs 15,000 crore. Eleven of those stocks posted the largest one‑year price drops, ranging from a 32.05% fall for Jaiprakash Power Ventures to a 47.43% fall for Intellect Design Arena, while fund ownership in each rose modestly during the same period.
stories.why: Shows that fund managers kept allocating capital to these small‑cap stocks despite recent price weakness, which may affect future liquidity and price support.

stories.title: Weary of war but with no sign of backing down, Kyiv faces another punishing winter
stories.summary: Something weird happens when you reach Kyiv after the eight-hour drive from the Polish border: the clock on your mobile phone goes to midnight. The war has dragged on for more than four and a half years, killing what some estimate could be 100,000 Ukrainian troops and 18,000 Ukrainian civilians, according to the United Nations, and probably more.

stories.title: Canada's top court largely upholds Quebec ban on religious symbols for public servants
stories.summary: Canada's top court has largely upheld a Quebec law banning public sector workers from wearing religious symbols, including the hijab and the cross. Quebec passed the law in 2019 under a unique fixture of Canada's constitution called the "notwithstanding clause" - a legal loophole that allows governments to override certain rights, like freedom of religion.

stories.title: RBI monitors gold‑loan market as bullion prices fall
stories.summary: The Reserve Bank of India said it is closely monitoring the gold‑loan segment after a decline in bullion prices raised concerns that existing collateral may become insufficient. The sector has grown rapidly, and the price drop could increase loan delinquencies. Lenders such as IIFL Finance and Bajaj Finance are already seeing repayment stress, and borrowers may be asked to provide additional security or repay loans.
